theorem_title: Target blindness is equivalent to a common-kernel witness
natural_language_statement:
Let $I,X,V$ be arbitrary types with distinguished zeros in $X,V$, subtraction operations, observation maps $r_i:X\to V$ and target $q:X\to V$. Assume the maps preserve zero and subtraction, and subtraction in $V$ is zero exactly when its arguments are equal. For a selected set $S\subseteq I$, let $K_S=\{d\in X:\forall i\in S,\ r_i(d)=0\}$.

$$
\bigl(\exists x,y\in X,\ q(x)\ne q(y)\ \land\ \forall i\in S,\ r_i(x)=r_i(y)\bigr)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists d\in K_S,\ q(d)\ne0.
$$

This difference-witness criterion applies to the stated subtraction-preserving interface. Linear maps satisfy that interface, but no vector-space or scalar-multiplication assumptions are needed.
